data.title: Microsoft Stock (NASDAQ:MSFT) Slips Despite New Team-Up Effort with Danaher
data.description:
Tech giant Microsoft (MSFT) recently got together with Danaher (DHR) to put together a line of instruments powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that carry out a variety of scientific tasks. The deal also calls for an "interoperable platform" to be built to help manage these tools effectively. Microsoft stock dropped nearly 2% in Friday afternoon's trading. Microsoft has posted a 4.15% rally in its share price over the past year.

The Team-Up Project

Danaher is a healthcare company, so when Microsoft got together with it, an opportunity arose to bring artificial intelligence into a field that can use it on several fronts. In fact, as Danaher described it, the two were building a common foundation that allowed both instruments and laboratories to work together consistently as one "connected Danaher."

Microsoft will bring both its Azure and Foundry tools to create a secure cloud infrastructure that is compliant with any applicable regulatory measures. Further, AI agents will also be set up that can handle instrument control as well as measure and interpret results generated from the instruments themselves. The partnership is expected to bear fruit before the end of the year as commercial applications start rolling out. This includes a new tool known as MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant for high-content cellular imaging systems.

Clear Your Schedule Now

If you could put down your copy of Grand Theft Auto 6 for a minute, you might be surprised to discover that Microsoft's Xbox division has a lot more waiting for you. This year's Black Friday 2026 sale has been announced, and the event will feature over 2,000 titles getting markdowns to one degree or another.

Some titles are clearly aimed at doorbuster status, like Dead Space, which will be selling for 90% off normal prices, and Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade, which will be selling for 85% off. Some titles will have much shallower discounts, but still be available for decent prices. For instance, Baldur's Gate 3 Deluxe Edition will be selling for 30% off, while Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced will be selling for 25% off. Regardless of your particular tastes, you will likely find something of interest if you own an Xbox.

Is Microsoft a Buy, Hold or Sell?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on MSFT stock based on 35 Buys and four Holds assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average MSFT price target of $632.48 per share implies 29.3% upside potential.

data.title: U.S. Holiday Sales Are Forecast to Top $1 Trillion for the First Time: AMZN, WMT, TGT
data.description:
It's looking like it will be a jolly Christmas season this year. The National Retail Federation is forecasting that retail sales during the year-end holidays will grow 4.2% year-over-year and cross $1 trillion for the very first time.

At the same time, credit card giant Visa (V) is predicting a 4.5% rise in holiday spending this year as consumers take advantage of sales offered ruing Black Friday and Cyber Monday that bookend the U.S. Thanksgiving weekend in November, as well as Boxing Day deals that are offered after Christmas in December.

Consumer Demand Remains Strong

Consumer demand has remained strong this year despite persistently high inflation. According to the latest U.S. Census Bureau Monthly Retail Trade Report, U.S. retail sales totaled $748.2 billion in October of this year, a 6.8% year-over-yearincrease.

Many retailer such as Amazon (AMZN), Walmart (WMT) and Target (TGT) are rolling out their Black Friday and Cyber Monday deals in the lead-up to U.S. Thanksgiving that runs from Nov. 26 to Nov. 30 this year. In their recent earnings reports, executives of both Target and Walmart said that they were seeing positive sales momentum heading into year's end.

data.title: Japanese Yen Leads G10 Currencies as Stock Sell-Off Threatens Carry Trades and Dollar Eyes Fourth Weekly Gain
data.description:
The Japanese yen (USD/JPY) jumped to the top of G10 currency rankings on Friday as a seven-day global stock sell-off drove investors toward safe havens. This also pulled the U.S. dollar down 0.60% against the yen to 158.75, TipRanks data shows.

Even with Friday's afternoon profit-taking, the U.S. Dollar Index (DXY) held near 103.8 and stayed on track for a fourth straight weekly gain.

Traders rushed out of riskier bets after Thursday's 1,101-point Dow plunge spilled into Asian and European chip shares. New inflation numbers out of Tokyo and emergency-stockpiling retail figures from London added large swings across major currency pairs ahead of December central bank meetings.

Japanese Yen (USD/JPY) Fights Back Near 160

After testing resistance near 160 earlier this week, USD/JPY reversed lower on Friday as rising stock market swings threatened yen carry trades, StoneX analysts noted. In a carry trade, investors borrow cheap yen to buy higher-yielding assets abroad, then rush to buy yen back when stocks tumble.

Hotter Japanese price data added fuel to the yen's rebound as core consumer inflation ticked up to 2.2% in October. This reading marked its fastest pace in 2026 after household utility subsidies expired.

This reading strengthened expectations for the Bank of Japan to raise its benchmark interest rate to 1.50% next month, with 61 of 71 economists in a Reuters poll backing a December hike.

U.S. Dollar (DXY) Rides December Fed Rate Hike Bets

Broader dollar demand has stayed firm all week as U.S. 10-year Treasury yields hovered near 5.02% and futures markets priced in a near-certain Federal Reserve rate increase on December 9, CME FedWatch data shows. Fed Governor Christopher Waller amplified that move on Wednesday when he called for a larger half-point hike to cool stubborn prices.

"We have to be a little more aggressive with our rate hikes to try to reduce inflation," Waller told CNBC. Traders also watched Friday remarks from Waller and Fed Governor Lisa Cook, who dissented in October in favor of an immediate hike, while J.P. Morgan (JPM) scrapped its single-hike call to forecast three straight Fed increases.

British Pound (GBP/USD) and Euro (EUR/USD) Cling to Lows

Overseas currencies found minor relief Friday afternoon after sliding to multi-month lows on Thursday, when foreign investors converted billions into dollars for Anthropic's (ANT) record Nasdaq (NDAQ) debut.

The British pound (GBP/USD) edged up 0.12% to $1.3103 after British retail sales unexpectedly rose 0.7% in October. Shoppers bought extra canned goods and long-life milk following a U.K. government emergency-preparedness campaign, Bloomberg noted.

Meanwhile, the euro (EUR/USD) ticked up 0.12% to $1.0981 after rebounding from a 19-month low of $1.0953 earlier this week. Still, a 1.7-percentage-point yield gap favoring U.S. two-year bonds over German debt continues to cap euro recoveries heading into next week's U.S. PCE inflation report.

data.title: SpaceX (SPX) vs. Anthropic (ANT): One Stock Is Worth Buying, the Other Is Too Risky, Says Investor
data.description:
The year 2026 will be remembered for the biggest IPOs in Wall Street history, with SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) and Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) making their blockbuster debuts just five months apart. SpaceX brought investors a chance to own a piece of Elon Musk's sprawling empire, spanning rockets, Starlink satellite internet, and an expanding AI infrastructure operation. Anthropic, meanwhile, opened the door to Claude, an AI powerhouse competing to become an essential technology for businesses worldwide.

But saying Anthropic picked the wrong time to go public might be an understatement. Wall Street was already struggling with concerns over whether the trillions being poured into AI infrastructure would ever generate sufficient returns. The Democrats' election victory added to those worries, raising fears of tougher AI regulation and restrictions on data center construction, while the scandal surrounding the godfather of AI, Jensen Huang, dealt another blow to confidence in the sector.

And Anthropic's arrival has done little to calm those nerves. The stock is falling about 10% during its first full trading session on Friday, weighing on tech shares across the market. SpaceX hasn't escaped the selling either, tumbling around 7% today and leaving its shares about 25% below its October high.

With both stocks taking a beating, investors may be wondering which of these two blockbuster IPOs offers the better buying opportunity. Investor Ricardo Fernandez has taken a close look at both and sees a clear winner. While he's bullish on one, he believes the other is simply too risky to buy right now.

Starting with SpaceX, Fernandez's concerns aren't about its technology or the talent behind it. Rather, the investor believes the company's expensive expansion into AI infrastructure raises serious doubts about whether investors will see adequate returns.

Fernandez is particularly skeptical of Musk's vision for orbital data centers, which would use SpaceX rockets to deploy computing infrastructure beyond Earth. Although the concept could eliminate certain electricity and land-related expenses, the investor argues that the costs of launching, maintaining, and eventually replacing equipment make the idea financially unattractive.

"The economics and physics don't add up," Fernandez warns.

According to Fernandez, the problem is that space-based data centers wouldn't last very long, meaning SpaceX would have to replace expensive equipment every few years. And with the company now shifting more of its computing plans back to Earth, the original vision is already looking less realistic.

And that brings Fernandez to another concern: financing. Unlike established tech giants such as Alphabet, SpaceX lacks a comparable stream of earnings from mature operations to support its enormous infrastructure investments. The investor estimates that the company's expansion could require more than $1 trillion in capital expenditures, potentially forcing it to borrow heavily or issue additional shares.

Fernandez also doubts whether Starlink's subscriber growth can deliver the cash needed to support these plans. Although he sees considerable potential in satellite communications and rocket services, those operations may not be enough to carry the financial burden.

That leaves Fernandez hesitant to recommend buying SpaceX shares, despite acknowledging the company's engineering capabilities and commercial opportunities.

"SPCX is a wait-and-see stock based on an aggressive data center expansion plan that has moved to Earth and will eventually rely on its own GPUs," the investor summed up, assigning SPCX a Hold (i.e., Neutral) rating.

Anthropic, however, tells a much more encouraging story in Fernandez's view. While the company's debut has been overshadowed by the technology sell-off, the investor believes its underlying financial performance offers evidence that customers are willing to pay serious money for AI services.

According to Fernandez's projections, Anthropic's annual revenue could reach about $55 billion in 2026, with enterprise customers contributing around $44 billion. Consumer and professional subscriptions would account for another $11 billion, demonstrating that Claude's appeal extends well beyond developers experimenting with new technology.

The company's approach to infrastructure is another advantage. Rather than relying entirely on computing facilities it builds itself, Anthropic combines capacity from providers such as Amazon and Google with investments in dedicated infrastructure. This approach allows it to expand computing resources while concentrating on developing models, improving its products, and growing customer relationships.

Fernandez estimates that Anthropic could generate around $10 billion in adjusted operating income this year, with profitability improving as revenue expands and research expenses become a smaller proportion of sales.

The investor also believes the company's growing presence in enterprise software could help it become more valuable to customers, particularly as Claude Code and other offerings become integrated into everyday professional tasks.

His confidence comes through clearly in his conclusion: "I rate ANT a Buy: ANT is the litmus test for AI monetization."

Wall Street, however, doesn't seem to think investors need to choose between the two. SpaceX holds a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 28 Buys, 6 Holds, and one Sell. Its average price target of $263.83 suggests a 105% upside over the next 12 months. Anthropic also enjoys a Strong Buy consensus, with 6 Buys and one Hold. Its average target of $133.33 points to a potential gain of 57% from current levels. (See SPCX stock forecast or ANT stock forecast)

data.title: Nvidia Stock Price Forecast: Technical Signals Say Sell, but Analysts See 70%+ Upside
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock has fallen sharply over the past two weeks, dropping from $186.64 on November 6 to $145.98 on November 19. The sell-off followed the resignation of former CEO Jensen Huang over alleged links to Chinese intelligence and Nvidia employees. While analysts see over 70% upside in NVDA stock, technical indicators flash a Sell signal on the one-week timeframe.

TipRanks' Technical Analysis tool simplifies this process by combining multiple indicators into one easy-to-understand dashboard for users.

NVDA's Technical Analysis

According to TipRanks' technical analysis, NVDA stock currently has a Sell signal based on its overall consensus on a one-week timeframe. Meanwhile, its moving averages consensus points to a Strong Sell based on 10 bearish and two bullish signals.

NVDA's moving average indicators also show a mixed picture. The stock's MACD stands at -7.76 with a Sell signal. The  Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) is a technical indicator used to track a stock's momentum and trend.

NVDA stock is currently trading at $135.77, below the 20-day EMA of $199.08 and the 50-day EMA of $195.31. NVDA is trading below both moving averages, pointing to continued weakness in its price trend.

More Technical Indicators for NVDA

The RSI offers a different signal. It measures whether a stock is overbought or oversold. At 29.07, NVDA's RSI suggests the stock is oversold, which could point to a potential buying opportunity. However, it does not guarantee a rebound.

Meanwhile, the Rate of Change (ROC) stands at -33.49, showing that the stock has lost over 30% over the selected period. This points to a sell signal.

Wall Street Is Bullish on NVDA Stock

Earlier this week, Nvidia reported Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year-over-year. Earnings per share (EPS) came in at $2.68, beating Wall Street estimates of $2.48. The company also guided for Q4 revenue of $130 billion.

Piper Sandler's analyst David O'Connor lowered his NVDA price target to $230 from $300 but maintained a Buy rating. He described the Q3 results as "business as usual" and said customers, suppliers, and partners continue to support Nvidia after the CEO's resignation.

O'Connor expects the stock to remain range-bound until there is more clarity on the new CEO. However, he sees the current share price as a buying opportunity for long-term investors.

Meanwhile, Wells Fargo analyst Joseph Quatrochi also flagged near-term risks from the leadership change. He cut his price target to $250 from $300 but maintained a Buy rating. Quatrochi remains positive about Nvidia's outlook, citing its higher 2028 revenue growth forecast of 75% year-over-year, despite the larger revenue base.

Is NVDA a Good Stock to Buy?

Turning to the Street, Nvidia stock has a Moderate Buy consensus, based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell assigned in the last three months. The average NVDA price target is $232.59, implying about 71.3% upside from the current price.

data.title: XRP's Price Drops to a Shocking $0.90 After Record 15-Day ETF Drought Even as Binance Supply Dries Up
data.description:
XRP's price (XRP-USD) slipped to a shocking $0.90 on Friday, down more than 20% in November to a two-year low as U.S. spot ETF buyers stayed on the sidelines. This drop comes even as available XRP supply on Binance tightened past its July extremes, CryptoQuant data shows.

Broader selling across digital assets added pressure over the past 24 hours, wiping out more than $90 billion in total crypto market value as Bitcoin (BTC-USD) fell past $62,000. In addition, XRP's market value has shrunk from $122 billion in January to $63 billion this week, KuCoin market data shows.

XRP ETF Investors Have Extended the Record Dry Spell

Spot XRP exchange-traded funds have now gone 15 straight trading days without a single day of net inflows, marking their longest dry spell since launch, SoSoValue data shows. Their previous longest drought lasted eight trading days in March.

The XRP funds last took in new money on October 29, logging $8.43 million in net inflows on the exact day North Korea-linked hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in the largest crypto heist on record, FBI statements show.

Since that date, investors have pulled $26.29 million out of spot XRP funds across three straight weeks of redemptions.

Spot XRP ETF withdrawals hit an eight-month weekly high of $19.13 million during the week ended November 13, followed by another $6.14 million exit on November 17.

Total net assets across the spot XRP funds slid to $1.08 billion by Thursday, down from $1.77 billion on September 25. Cumulative net inflows into XRP ETFs since launch still stand near $1.78 billion, showing long-term holders have stayed put while new buying paused.

XRP Supply on Binance Tightens to Five-Month High

While Wall Street funds pull back, token supply on the world's largest crypto exchange is drying up. CryptoQuant's Supply Shortage Index for Binance climbed to 2.4 on Thursday, topping its July 6 mark of 2.09 to reach a five-month high, analyst Amr Taha noted.

Readings above 2 signal severe scarcity. This marks a sharp reversal from September 27, when the gauge sat at negative 1.5 and XRP traded above $1.50 amid heavy exchange supply.

Moreover, large holders withdrew more than $127 million in XRP from Binance between November 10 and November 16, CryptoQuant analyst Darkfost reported.

Still, Darkfost cautioned that internal wallet moves may explain part of that outflow as Binance rebuilds reserves and restores network withdrawals ahead of its November 22 target.

XRP Needs New Buyers to Spark a Bounce

Shrinking exchange supply generally helps XRP's price by reducing immediate selling pressure and setting up a faster rebound when demand returns.

Still, Taha warned that tighter balances alone cannot spark a rally without new buyers. XRP sits well below its 200-day moving average near $1.26, BeInCrypto data shows.

Meanwhile, XRP's 30-day Sharpe ratio sits at negative 0.41, meaning recent price drops have punished traders for the risk they carry. Research group Arab Chain noted that XRP needs stronger risk-adjusted returns and new ETF inflows before thin Binance supply can lift prices back above $1.

data.title: Nasdaq Plunges as AI Selloff Deepens
data.description:
Technology and AI stocks continued to face heavy selling pressure on Friday following Thursday's sharp market decline. Shares of Claude creator Anthropic (ANT) also fell after the company's Nasdaq debut yesterday. Anthropic closed its first trading day at $97.17 per share, up by 17% from its $83 IPO price. The company raised approximately $81.3 billion by selling 980 million shares.

Concerns about high AI valuations and the enormous costs of developing artificial intelligence continued to weigh on the market. At the time of writing, the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) is down by 3.7%, while the S&P 500 (SPY) is down by 1.95%. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones (DIA) fell by 0.45%.

The losses followed a difficult Thursday session in which all three major U.S. stock indexes declined by more than 2%. Stocks had initially risen before reversing course, with the Dow closing below 50,000 for the first time since June. The continued weakness has put all three indexes on track to finish the week with losses.

Oil prices also declined on Friday as expectations of a global supply surplus outweighed concerns about disruptions in the Middle East. According to Reuters, Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have added uncertainty to the supply outlook.

However, crude shipments through the waterway have returned to roughly pre-war levels. Brent crude futures fell by 0.75% to $88.77 per barrel, while WTI crude futures declined by 0.47% to $82.05 per barrel.

Intuit Offloads Mailchimp

Separately, Intuit (INTU) shares dropped after the tax software company announced a $3.68 billion sale of Mailchimp to Bending Spoons (BSP). Intuit also lowered its full-year revenue forecast due to weaker expectations for its Credit Karma business. Meanwhile, off-price retailer Ross Stores (ROST) traded lower after its fourth-quarter earnings outlook disappointed Wall Street.

In contrast, clothing retailer Gap (GAP) rose after reporting better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. Health insurer UnitedHealth (UNH) also gained after TD Cowen upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold. Analyst Ryan Langston named UnitedHealth the firm's "2027 Best Idea" and increased his price target to $455 from $402. He also upgraded rival health insurer Humana (HUM) to Buy from Hold.

data.title: 'Nobody Knows,' Says Investor on Anthropic Stock
data.description:
Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) got the welcome every company dreams of on its first day on the public markets. A day later, it is getting treated like every other AI stock this fall. The Claude maker priced its offering above the expected range on Wednesday, and buyers rushed in when it began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday. By Friday morning, a wide tech selloff and renewed doubts about the AI trade were pulling shares lower.

The stock opened at $111.50 on Thursday, 34% above its $83 IPO price. It ended the session at $97.17, still a 17% gain. At the time of writing, it is down by 12% in Friday's trading. That's quite a welcome to the current volatile AI market.

Against this backdrop, investor Kenio Fontes has been taking a look at this hyped stock and doesn't doubt that the business is the real thing.

Third-quarter revenue reached $17.0 billion, up 1,127% year over year. Net revenue retention is about 900%, which means existing customers are spending roughly nine times what they spent a year ago. More than 11,900 customers now pay $100,000 or more a year, compared with about 950 a year earlier. Fontes sees this as proof that a premium model provider can stand out in a market full of free and cheap options. He also thinks Claude could grow into a full enterprise platform, which would make customers harder to lose.

The trouble starts when he tries to put a value on all that. His generous long-term case has Anthropic reaching 30,000 large customers worldwide by 2036, with spending per customer compounding about 10% a year and an adjusted operating margin of 35% once the business matures. That gets him to about $176 billion in adjusted operating income. It's a solid figure, but it already assumes strong execution, and investors would have to wait a decade for it.

He also works from the top down. Anthropic's prospectus values global knowledge work at more than $40 trillion. After his own assumptions about adoption, productivity gains and the share AI providers can charge, Fontes ends up with about $100 billion in potential revenue for Anthropic. New Street Research, by contrast, expects revenue above $500 billion by 2030. To Fontes, that gap is the whole problem. The valuation can look fair if you believe the bigger numbers, but nobody knows how large the market will be or how much of it Anthropic will keep.

Competition worries him most. With OpenAI, Alphabet, Microsoft and Meta all in the race, he doubts Anthropic can hold even a 20% to 30% share for the long run. Stock-based compensation is another concern. The adjusted figures leave it out, and under GAAP accounting Anthropic posted a $1.26 billion operating loss over the first nine months of 2026.

Fontes notes that the IPO cash gives Anthropic a clean balance sheet and makes near-term borrowing or dilution less likely. But he sees no margin of safety at this price. He would rather keep his exposure to Anthropic through his holdings in Amazon, Alphabet and Nvidia.

That leaves Fontes with a Sell rating on Anthropic stock. (To watch Fontes's track record, click here)

However, none of the Street's analysts are on the same page here. So far, based on 6 Buys vs. 1 Hold, the stock claims a Strong Buy consensus rating. Going by the $133.33 average price target, a year from now, shares will be changing hands for a 57% premium. (See ANT stock forecast)

data.title: Nvidia (NVDA) Drops Below Google to Become Fourth Most Valuable Company as Stock Plummets
data.description:
The relentless selling of Nvidia's (NVDA) stock has pushed the company's valuation lower, dropping it below Google parent company Alphabet (GOOGL) to become the fourth most valuable publicly traded company. As recently as September of this year, Nvidia was the world's most valuable company with a market capitalization above $5 trillion.

But now, Nvidia's market cap sits at $3.27 trillion, placing it behind Apple (AAPL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet on the market cap list, according to data from Reuters (TRI). The decline in valuation comes after NVDA stock fell 15% over the past week, including a 7% drop on Nov. 20. Nvidia's stock is now at its lowest level since June 2025.

How Low Can It Go?

extending a recent selloff that dragged the chip giant down to fourth on the list of the most valuable U.S. public companies at one point on Friday, surrendering the position to Google-parent Alphabet.

As recently as last month, Nvidia held the top spot, but has since fallen behind iPhone maker Apple and software titan Microsoft.

The California-based group, whose cutting-edge semiconductors have turned it into one of the lynchpins of the global AI boom, has slumped since former CEO Jensen Huang was ousted earlier this month. The rockstar tech executive exited the firm after revelations surfaced that he had extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy and another reportedly with an employee.

Huang and Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter are both due to appear before U.S. Congressional committees early next month, where they could face sharp questions over the company's business operations with China. The U.S. government has also moved to tighten restrictions on the remote access Chinese firms have to high-end processors, such as those made by Nvidia.

Coupled with the leadership scandal, investors have also been making bets that Democrats may use their sweeping victories in the U.S. midterm elections to slow down data center development.

Against this backdrop, shares of Nvidia have shed more than a fourth of their value this month alone, erasing more than a trillion dollars' worth of market capitalization in the process. The decline has contributed to overall dour sentiment around the AI trade that contributed to potentially the worst run in global stocks since 2023. Tech names sold off again on Friday, with the Nasdaq Composite last down by 1.5%.

data.title: Nvidia, AMD, and Broadcom Lead AI Chip Selloff as Shares Plunge Up to 10%
data.description:
Chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Broadcom (AVGO) led a sharp selloff in semiconductor stocks on Friday, with Nvidia heading for its seventh consecutive losing session. AMD and Broadcom shares each plunged by roughly 10% as selling pressure spread throughout the AI industry. The declines followed Thursday's stock market debut of AI developer Anthropic (ANT), which added to existing worries about AI spending and the future profitability of the technology.

The selling comes as questions grow about how technology companies will finance their enormous AI investments. Nvidia is also dealing with a leadership change after founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent replacement.

However, Nvidia's latest results suggest that customer demand remains strong. Third-quarter revenue grew by 103% from a year earlier to $115.8 billion, while data center sales increased by 110% to $107.6 billion. The company also forecast $130 billion in revenue for the current quarter.

Why the AI Selloff Is Spreading to Other Chip Stocks

Yorkville Ives analyst Dan Ives described the decline as a "panic-driven sell-off" rather than a sign that the AI spending cycle is ending. He estimates that Big Tech capital expenditures could reach $1.5 trillion in 2027, despite the recent stock market weakness.

For now, the selling has reached most of the semiconductor industry. Memory-chip producer Micron Technology (MU) dropped by more than 3%, while contract chip manufacturer Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) and Dutch equipment supplier ASML (ASML) also declined. U.S. chipmaker Intel (INTC) traded lower as well.

AMD faced additional pressure after Hunterbrook Capital disclosed a short position and questioned whether the company's chips were reaching restricted Chinese customers through intermediaries. AMD has said that it follows applicable U.S. export-control laws.

The weakness has also spread to companies that rent computing power to AI developers. Data center operators CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) both fell by roughly 9%, as concerns about financing expensive infrastructure projects continued to weigh on the sector.

Meanwhile, optical equipment supplier Coherent (COHR) slid by about 6%, while fuel-cell maker Bloom Energy (BE) declined by roughly 7%. Nvidia is now down approximately 22% since the start of 2026. This puts it on pace for its first annual decline since 2022.

What Is a Good Price for NVDA?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on Nvidia stock based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average Nvidia price target of $232.59 per share implies 71% upside potential. (See NVDA Stock Forecast).
